thread.title_full: Docs: Ax used to kill man in Portsmouth - NewsBreak

author: Dana Hazzard
title: Docs: Ax used to kill man in Portsmouth - NewsBreak
text:
By Dana Hazzard Brett Hall ,
4 hours ago
PORTSMOUTH, Va. (WAVY) — A man charged with first-degree murder used an ax to strike and kill his victim before burning the body and placing it in a ditch, according to a Portsmouth Police probable cause statement.
Gregory Coffey, 53, was arraigned Thursday morning in Portsmouth General District Court in connection to the death of 47-year-old Gordon Randolph Tillman Jr. Aside from the murder charge, he faces a count of defiling a dead, human body. He is being held without bail.
The crime happened Aug. 30, according to court documents, and a detective's affidavit states two different people witnessed the killing.
Coffey told both that Tillman had been stealing from him.
"He won't steal none of my s*** anymore," Coffey allegedly told a witness to the killing, according to detectives.
PPD find human remains in backyard of Elliott Ave. home, homeowner charged with murder Tillman was reported missing by his brother Raymond Poole on Sept. 2, police detailed during a press conference Wednesday. Tillman frequently visited Coffey's residence at 3414 Elliott Ave. in the Highland Biltmore area of the city.
It was a citizen's tip and further investigative work that led police to execute a search warrant at the home Sept. 22.
Court documents revealed that the person who provided the tip contacted police on Sept. 21 and stated that she had knowledge of the location of a dead body at the Elliott Avenue property, and that the decedent was a missing person. She further said Coffey asked her son for help in concealing and burning the decedent's body, which the son refused.
Two witnesses told detectives they witnessed Coffey strike Tillman in the head and body with an ax at his residence on Elliott Avenue.
A witness interviewed by detectives said that Coffey made statements in reference to Tillman stealing from him on a prior occasion. One witness said that after Coffey struck Tillman with the ax, Coffey said Tillman wouldn't steal from him anymore, and that he "can't let him get out of here like that — I'll go to jail for life."
Police say remains were found adjacent to the property and turned over to the Virginia Office of the Chief Medical Examiner, who later confirmed they were human.
Fingerprints positively identified those remains as that of Gordon Randolph Tillman Jr.
“Unfortunately, Mr. Tillman was dismembered,” Portsmouth Police Chief Stephen Jenkins said. “Parts of his body were burned and decomposed.”
One witness said they placed the ax on the left side of the garage so Coffey couldn't use it on them. While executing the search warrant, law enforcement officials recovered the ax from that location.
Documents also revealed that Coffey burned Tillman's body and asked a witness to apply chemicals to prevent an odor and decomposition.
Upon searching the property, law enforcement officials located large areas of blood and burned bone fragments. Multiple marks were found on the ceiling and walls of the garage, consistent with an ax.
Documents also reveal FBI agents located the heavily decomposed body in a ditch underneath a sheet of plywood near Elliott Street and Woodstock Street.
Coffey's next court appearance is set for November.
